name: Fair Tax Foundation
summary: A not-for-profit community benefit society in Manchester (Fair Tax Foundation Limited, FCA no. 32308R, with an asset lock; not a registered charity, so gifts get no Gift Aid) that runs the Fair Tax Mark, a certification of responsible tax conduct held by 275 businesses paying GBP 4.1 billion a year in corporate income tax, and the Tax Responsibility and Transparency Index for multinationals. It also runs Fair Tax Week and the Councils for Fair Tax Declaration and campaigns for public country-by-country reporting in the UK. Fees from certified businesses are 90% of its income; it accepts donations. It spent GBP 451,698 in 2025, with 7.6 staff.

spending.source: https://fairtaxmark.net/wp-content/uploads/Annual-Report-and-Accounts-2025.pdf (financial statements for the year ended 31 December 2025, unaudited under the audit exemption of s84 of the Co-operative and Community Benefit Societies Act 2014, independent reporting accountant's report; revenue account p. 12: administrative expenses GBP 451,698, the accounts' one line of costs; at the IRS 2025 average of 1.3175 dollars per pound)
